A circle has infinitely many tangents, one at each point."},{"k":"box","kind":"definition","title":"Theorem: tangent ⟂ radius","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The tangent at any point of a circle is **perpendicular** to the radius drawn to the point of contact."},{"k":"p","text":"*Proof.* Let $L$ touch the circle at $A$, and let $B$ be any other point of $L$. $B$ lies outside the circle, so $OB$ crosses the circle at some point $C$, and $OB=OC+CB>OC=OA$. So $OA$ is the shortest distance from $O$ to $L$. The shortest segment from a point to a line is the perpendicular, so $OA\\perp L$. $\\blacksquare$"}]},{"k":"fig","id":"w11-perp","caption":"$OA$ is the shortest distance from $O$ to $L$."},{"k":"p","text":"Conversely, a line through a point of the circle that is perpendicular to the radius there is a tangent. To **construct the tangent at $A$**, draw the radius $OA$, extend it, and construct the perpendicular to $OA$ at $A$."}],"figs":["w11-perp"]},{"title":"Tangents from an external point","blocks":[{"k":"box","kind":"definition","title":"Theorem: equal tangents","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The two tangents drawn to a circle from an external point $P$ are **equal** in length: $PA=PB$. Moreover, $OP$ **bisects** $\\angle APB$ and $\\angle AOB$, and $OP$ is the **perpendicular bisector** of the chord of contact $AB$."},{"k":"p","text":"*Proof.* In triangles $OAP$ and $OBP$: $\\angle OAP=\\angle OBP=90^\\circ$ (tangent ⟂ radius), $OP$ is a common hypotenuse and $OA=OB$ (radii). So the triangles are congruent (RHS), giving $PA=PB$, $\\angle APO=\\angle BPO$ and $\\angle AOP=\\angle BOP$. $\\blacksquare$"}]},{"k":"fig","id":"w11-equal","caption":"Two congruent right-angled triangles."},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Useful results","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["Tangent length from $P$: $PA^2=OP^2-r^2$.","In quadrilateral $OAPB$: $\\angle AOB+\\angle APB=180^\\circ$ (two right angles).","Triangle $PAB$ is isosceles, so $\\angle PAB=\\angle PBA=\\dfrac{180^\\circ-\\angle APB}{2}$."]}]},{"k":"p","text":"To **construct the tangents from $P$**: bisect $OP$ at $M$ and draw the circle with centre $M$ through $O$ and $P$. It cuts the given circle at $A$ and $B$, and $PA$, $PB$ are the tangents, because $\\angle OAP$ and $\\angle OBP$ are angles in a semicircle."},{"k":"fig","id":"w11-construct","caption":"The circle on $OP$ as diameter gives the points of contact."}],"figs":["w11-equal","w11-construct"]},{"title":"The alternate segment theorem","blocks":[{"k":"box","kind":"definition","title":"Theorem: alternate segment","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The angle between a tangent and a chord drawn through the point of contact equals the angle subtended by the chord in the **alternate segment** (the segment on the other side of the chord)."}]},{"k":"fig","id":"w11-altproof","caption":"Proof of the alternate segment theorem."},{"k":"box","kind":"key","title":"Proof","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Let $DAE$ be the tangent at $A$, $AB$ the chord, $\\angle BAE=x$, and $C$ a point in the alternate segment. $\\angle OAE=90^\\circ$, so $\\angle OAB=90^\\circ-x$. $OA=OB$, so $\\angle OBA=90^\\circ-x$ and $\\angle AOB=180^\\circ-2(90^\\circ-x)=2x$. By the angle-at-the-centre theorem, $\\angle ACB=\\tfrac12\\angle AOB=x$. $\\blacksquare$"}]},{"k":"p","text":"In a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ with tangent $DAE$ at $A$, the theorem combines with the opposite-angle theorem: each angle between the tangent and a side equals the angle at the far vertex across that side."}],"figs":["w11-altproof"]},{"title":"Inscribed circles and common tangents","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The **inscribed circle** (incircle) of a triangle touches all three sides; its centre, the **incentre**, is where the angle bisectors meet. In triangles $OAP$ and $OBP$: $\\angle OAP=\\angle OBP=90^\\circ$ (tangent ⟂ radius), $OP$ is common, and $OA=OB$ (radii). So the triangles are congruent (RHS) and $PA=PB$."},{"k":"p","text":"(b) From the congruence, $\\angle APO=\\angle BPO$, so $PO$ bisects $\\angle APB$ (and $\\angle AOP=\\angle BOP$)."},{"k":"p","text":"(c) Let $OP$ meet $AB$ at $M$. Hence $AM=BM$ and $\\angle AMP=\\angle BMP$; these angles are equal and add to $180^\\circ$, so each is $90^\\circ$. (c) If $x=25^\\circ$ and the radius is 8 cm, find $TA$.","steps":[],"answer":"","model":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) $\\angle AOB=180^\\circ-2x$; $\\angle ACB=\\tfrac12(180^\\circ-2x)=90^\\circ-x$; $\\angle TAB=\\dfrac{180^\\circ-2x}{2}=90^\\circ-x$."},{"k":"p","text":"(b) Both equal $90^\\circ-x$. $TA$ is a tangent and $AB$ a chord, and $C$ is in the alternate segment: this is the alternate segment theorem."},{"k":"p","text":"(c) $\\angle ATO=x=25^\\circ$, and in right triangle $OAT$: $\\tan25^\\circ=\\dfrac{8}{TA}$, so $TA=\\dfrac{8}{\\tan25^\\circ}\\approx17.16$ cm."}]},{"q":"(a) Prove the alternate segment theorem. (b) In the figure, $PQ$ is a tangent at $A$, $ABCD$ is cyclic, $\\angle PAD=50^\\circ$, $\\angle QAB=62^\\circ$ and $\\angle BDC=28^\\circ$. Find $\\angle ABD$, $\\angle ADB$, $\\angle BAD$, $\\angle BAC$ and $\\angle BCD$.","steps":[],"answer":"","model":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) As in the notes: with $\\angle BAE=x$, $\\angle OAB=90^\\circ-x$, $\\angle OBA=90^\\circ-x$, so $\\angle AOB=2x$, and the angle in the alternate segment is $\\tfrac12\\angle AOB=x$."},{"k":"p","text":"(b) $\\angle ABD=\\angle PAD=50^\\circ$ (alternate segment, chord $AD$). $\\angle ADB=\\angle QAB=62^\\circ$ (alternate segment, chord $AB$). $\\angle BAD=180^\\circ-50^\\circ-62^\\circ=68^\\circ$. $\\angle BAC=\\angle BDC=28^\\circ$ (same segment, chord $BC$). $\\angle BCD=180^\\circ-68^\\circ=112^\\circ$ (opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral)."}]},{"q":"A bicycle has a front chain wheel of radius 9 cm and a rear sprocket of radius 3 cm, with centres 40 cm apart. The chain runs round both along the two direct common tangents. (a) Find the length of each straight part of the chain. (b) Find the angle $\\theta$ that each radius to a point of contact makes with the line of centres. (c) Hence find the total length of the chain, to the nearest centimetre.","steps":[],"answer":"","model":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) $\\sqrt{40^2-(9-3)^2}=\\sqrt{1564}\\approx39.55$ cm."},{"k":"p","text":"(b) $\\cos\\theta=\\dfrac{9-3}{40}=0.15$, so $\\theta\\approx81.37^\\circ$."},{"k":"p","text":"(c) On the large wheel the chain wraps the arc away from the small wheel: angle $360^\\circ-2\\theta\\approx197.25^\\circ$; on the small wheel it wraps $2\\theta\\approx162.75^\\circ$."},{"k":"p","text":"Arcs: $\\dfrac{197.25}{360}\\times2\\pi\\times9\\approx30.98$ cm and $\\dfrac{162.75}{360}\\times2\\pi\\times3\\approx8.52$ cm."},{"k":"p","text":"Total $\\approx2\\times39.55+30.98+8.52\\approx118.6$, about 119 cm."}]},{"q":"A right-angled triangle has legs $a$ and $b$ and hypotenuse $c$. (a) Show that the radius of its inscribed circle is $r=\\dfrac{a+b-c}{2}$ by using equal tangents. (b) Check the formula for the 3–4–5 triangle and the 5–12–13 triangle. (c) A triangular plot has sides 20 m, 21 m and 29 m. Find the radius of the largest circular fountain that fits inside it.","steps":[],"answer":"","model":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) At the right angle the two tangent lengths and two radii form a square of side $r$. So the tangent lengths from the acute vertices are $a-r$ and $b-r$, and these add up to the hypotenuse: $(a-r)+(b-r)=c$, giving $r=\\dfrac{a+b-c}{2}$."},{"k":"p","text":"(b) $3$–$4$–$5$: $r=\\dfrac{3+4-5}{2}=1$. $5$–$12$–$13$: $r=\\dfrac{5+12-13}{2}=2$. Both agree with $r=\\dfrac{\\text{area}}{s}$ ($\\tfrac66=1$ and $\\tfrac{30}{15}=2$)."},{"k":"p","text":"(c) $20^2+21^2=841=29^2$, so the plot is right-angled. $r=\\dfrac{20+21-29}{2}=6$ m."}]}],"checklist":["I can prove and use: tangent ⟂ radius.","I can prove and use: tangents from an external point are equal.","I can construct the tangent at a point and the tangents from an external point.","I can prove and apply the alternate segment theorem.","I can find tangent lengths, angles and perimeters with Pythagoras and trigonometry.","I can solve problems on inscribed circles and on belts over pulleys."],"plan":{"lessons":[[{"j":0,"notes":true,"exs":[0]},{"j":1,"notes":true,"exs":[1,2,3,4,5]}],[{"j":1,"notes":false,"exs":[6]},{"j":2,"notes":true,"exs":[7]},{"j":3,"notes":true,"exs":[8,9,10,11]}]],"exSec":[0,1,1,1,1,1,1,2,3,3,3,3],"quizSec":[1,0,1,1,2,1,3,3,3,1],"exerSec":[0,1,1,2,1,3,3,3,2,3,0,1],"thSec":[1,1,2,3,3],"sumSec":[0,1,1,2,3,3],"chkSec":[0,1,1,2,1,3],"weights":[1688.4,5680.6,1837.8,4050.55],"figs":[{"id":"w11-perp","sec":0,"lesson":1,"caption":"$OA$ is the shortest distance from $O$ to $L$."},{"id":"w11-altproof","sec":2,"lesson":2,"caption":"Proof of the alternate segment theorem."}]},"next":"Geometric Construction I: Constructing Angles, Triangles and Bearings","tm":{"sectionNo":3,"sectionName":"Circle Theorems and Geometric Construction","strand":"Geometry Around Us","sub":"Spatial Sense","cs":["Demonstrate a conceptual understanding of spatial sense with respect to circles and their theorems, and apply their properties to solve everyday life problems."],"lo":["Draw circles for given radii and use the circle theorems; A protractor may be used only to **check** an answer afterwards."},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"Good practice","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["Use a sharp pencil and keep the compasses firm, so the radius does not slip.","**Leave all construction arcs** on the drawing: they are the evidence of the construction and earn marks.","Draw arcs long enough to cross clearly; label the points you use.","State measurements to the nearest millimetre or degree."]}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"The basic constructions","blocks":[{"k":"fig","id":"w12-basic","caption":"Four basic constructions."},{"k":"box","kind":"key","title":"Why they work","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["**Perpendicular bisector of $AB$:** arcs of equal radius from $A$ and $B$ meet at points equidistant from $A$ and $B$; the line through them is the perpendicular bisector.","**Angle bisector:** an arc from the vertex $O$ cuts the arms at $U$ and $V$ with $OU=OV$; equal arcs from $U$ and $V$ meet at $Z$. Triangles $OUZ$ and $OVZ$ are congruent (SSS), so $\\angle UOZ=\\angle VOZ$.","**Perpendicular from a point $P$ to a line** (or at a point on a line): an arc from $P$ cuts the line at $X$ and $Y$; the perpendicular bisector of $XY$ passes through $P$.","**60°:** with the same radius, arcs from $O$ and from $X$ meet at $Y$, so $OX=XY=OY$: triangle $OXY$ is equilateral and $\\angle XOY=60^\\circ$."]}]}],"figs":["w12-basic"]},{"title":"Building other angles","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"All the standard angles come from **60°** (stepping the radius once), **120°** (stepping it twice), **90°** (a perpendicular) and **bisection**."},{"k":"table","head":["Angle","Construction"],"rows":[["$30^\\circ$, $15^\\circ$","bisect $60^\\circ$, then bisect again"],["$45^\\circ$, $22\\tfrac12^\\circ$","bisect $90^\\circ$, then bisect again"],["$75^\\circ$","bisect between $60^\\circ$ and $90^\\circ$"],["$105^\\circ$","bisect between $90^\\circ$ and $120^\\circ$"],["$135^\\circ$","bisect between $90^\\circ$ and $180^\\circ$"],["$150^\\circ$","bisect between $120^\\circ$ and $180^\\circ$, or $90^\\circ+60^\\circ$"],["$165^\\circ$","bisect between $150^\\circ$ and $180^\\circ$"]]},{"k":"fig","id":"w12-150","caption":"Constructing $150^\\circ$."},{"k":"fig","id":"w12-75","caption":"Constructing $75^\\circ$."},{"k":"fig","id":"w12-105","caption":"Constructing $105^\\circ$."},{"k":"fig","id":"w12-135","caption":"Constructing $135^\\circ$."},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Which angles can be constructed?","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"By halving and adding, every multiple of $15^\\circ$ can be constructed, and so can the halves of these: every multiple of $7\\tfrac12^\\circ$ (for example $37\\tfrac12^\\circ=\\tfrac12\\times75^\\circ$, $52\\tfrac12^\\circ=\\tfrac12\\times105^\\circ$, $97\\tfrac12^\\circ=90^\\circ+7\\tfrac12^\\circ$). An angle such as $80^\\circ$ or $40^\\circ$ cannot be constructed exactly with these methods."}]},{"k":"fig","id":"w12-fan","caption":"Every multiple of $15^\\circ$ from $60^\\circ$, $90^\\circ$, $120^\\circ$ and bisection."}],"figs":["w12-150","w12-75","w12-105","w12-135","w12-fan"]},{"title":"Constructing triangles and quadrilaterals","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A triangle is fixed by **SSS**, **SAS**, **ASA** (or AAS) or **RHS**. To construct one:"},{"k":"ol","items":["Make a **rough sketch** with all the given data.","Draw the base of the given length.","Construct the given angles at its ends (or draw arcs of the given lengths).","Mark the third vertex where the lines or arcs meet; join up.","Measure the required lengths or angles, and **check by calculation** when possible."]},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Checking by calculation","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["Angle sum: $A+B+C=180^\\circ$.","Sine rule: $\\dfrac{a}{\\sin A}=\\dfrac{b}{\\sin B}=\\dfrac{c}{\\sin C}$.","Cosine rule: $a^2=b^2+c^2-2bc\\cos A$."]}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Bearings","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A **bearing** is an angle measured **clockwise from north**, written with three figures ($075^\\circ$, $135^\\circ$). The **back bearing** differs from the bearing by $180^\\circ$."},{"k":"box","kind":"life","title":"Constructions at work","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Carpenters, masons and tailors set out right angles and $45^\\circ$ cuts with string and pegs or compasses; surveyors and navigators draw bearings to scale; engineers and architects still use construction to check computer drawings; and roof trusses commonly use $30^\\circ$, $45^\\circ$ and $60^\\circ$ angles."}]}],"figs":[]}],"examples":[{"title":"Constructing 150° in two ways","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Describe two ways of constructing an angle of $150^\\circ$ at a point $O$ on a straight line, and explain why each gives $150^\\circ$."}],"steps":["**Method 1.** With centre $O$ draw a large arc cutting the line at $X$ (on the right) and $W$ (on the left). With the same radius, step from $X$ to $Y_1$ and then to $Y_2$ on the arc. $\\angle XOY_2=120^\\circ$.","Bisect $\\angle Y_2OW$ (which is $60^\\circ$): equal arcs from $Y_2$ and $W$ meet at $Z$. Then $\\angle XOZ=120^\\circ+30^\\circ=150^\\circ$.","**Method 2.** Construct $OS\\perp$ the line at $O$, so $\\angle XOS=90^\\circ$. With the radius $OS$, arc from $S$ to cut the main arc on the left at $T$: triangle $OST$ is equilateral, so $\\angle SOT=60^\\circ$ and $\\angle XOT=90^\\circ+60^\\circ=150^\\circ$.","Check either with a protractor."],"answer":"$150^\\circ=120^\\circ+\\tfrac12(60^\\circ)$ or $90^\\circ+60^\\circ$.","figs":[]},{"title":"Constructing 75°","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Construct an angle of $75^\\circ$ at $O$ and explain each step."}],"steps":["Draw a line through $O$. With centre $O$ draw an arc cutting it at $X$.","With the same radius step from $X$ to $Y$: $\\angle XOY=60^\\circ$.","Construct the perpendicular $ON$ at $O$: $\\angle XON=90^\\circ$; let it cut the arc at $N$.","Bisect $\\angle YON$ ($30^\\circ$) with equal arcs from $Y$ and $N$, meeting at $Z$.","$\\angle XOZ=60^\\circ+15^\\circ=75^\\circ$."],"answer":"$75^\\circ=60^\\circ+\\tfrac12(90^\\circ-60^\\circ)$","figs":[]},{"title":"Constructing 105°","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Construct an angle of $105^\\circ$ at $O$."}],"steps":["Draw the line and the arc with centre $O$, cutting it at $X$.","Step the radius twice from $X$ to get the ray at $120^\\circ$.","Construct the perpendicular at $O$ to get the ray at $90^\\circ$.","Bisect the $30^\\circ$ angle between the $90^\\circ$ and $120^\\circ$ rays.","The bisector makes $90^\\circ+15^\\circ=105^\\circ$ with $OX$."],"answer":"$105^\\circ=90^\\circ+\\tfrac12(120^\\circ-90^\\circ)$","figs":[]},{"title":"135° and 165°","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Explain how to construct (a) $135^\\circ$ (b) $165^\\circ$."}],"steps":["(a) Construct the perpendicular at $O$ ($90^\\circ$). Bisect the right angle between it and the left-hand part of the line ($180^\\circ$): the bisector is at $90^\\circ+45^\\circ=135^\\circ$.","(b) First construct $150^\\circ$ (Example 12.1). Then bisect the $30^\\circ$ angle between the $150^\\circ$ ray and the left-hand part of the line: $150^\\circ+15^\\circ=165^\\circ$."],"answer":"(a) bisect between $90^\\circ$ and $180^\\circ$ (b) bisect between $150^\\circ$ and $180^\\circ$","figs":[]},{"title":"Halves of standard angles","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Plan the construction of (a) $22\\tfrac12^\\circ$ (b) $67\\tfrac12^\\circ$ (c) $37\\tfrac12^\\circ$ (d) $52\\tfrac12^\\circ$."}],"steps":["(a) Construct $90^\\circ$, bisect to get $45^\\circ$, bisect again: $22\\tfrac12^\\circ$.","(b) Construct $45^\\circ$ and $90^\\circ$ on the same side; bisect between them: $45^\\circ+22\\tfrac12^\\circ=67\\tfrac12^\\circ$.","(c) Construct $75^\\circ$ and bisect it: $37\\tfrac12^\\circ$.","(d) Construct $105^\\circ$ and bisect it: $52\\tfrac12^\\circ$."],"answer":"(a) $\\tfrac14$ of $90^\\circ$ (b) between $45^\\circ$ and $90^\\circ$ (c) $\\tfrac12$ of $75^\\circ$ (d) $\\tfrac12$ of $105^\\circ$","figs":[]},{"title":"Can it be constructed?","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Which of these angles can be constructed exactly with ruler and compasses using the methods above? (c) Points equidistant from the walls $AB$ and $AD$ of a room. (d) Points 2 m from a straight fence. Construct the locus $d$ of points equidistant from $m_1$ and $m_2$, and explain why it works."}],"steps":["At any point $O$ on $m_1$ construct the perpendicular, meeting $m_2$ at $A$.","Construct the perpendicular bisector of $OA$; call it $d$.","$d$ is perpendicular to $OA$, which is perpendicular to both lines, so $d$ is parallel to $m_1$ and $m_2$.","Every point of $d$ is at distance $\\tfrac12 OA$ from each line, so $d$ is the required locus."],"answer":"The perpendicular bisector of a common perpendicular $OA$.","figs":[]},{"title":"A parallelogram with two loci","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Construct parallelogram $PQRS$ with $PQ=8$ cm, $QR=6$ cm and diagonal $PR=11.5$ cm. (b) Construct the locus $u$ of points 5 cm from $Q$. (c) Construct the locus $t$ of points equidistant from $PS$ and $SR$. (d) Label the intersections of $u$ and $t$ as $A$ and $B$ and measure $AB$."}],"steps":["(a) Construct triangle $PQR$ by SSS. With centre $R$ and radius 8 cm, and centre $P$ and radius 6 cm, draw arcs meeting at $S$. Join $PS$ and $RS$.","(b) $u$ is the circle with centre $Q$ and radius 5 cm.","(c) $t$ is the bisector of $\\angle PSR$.","(d) $t$ cuts $u$ at $A$ (inside the parallelogram) and at $B$ (below $PQ$).","Calculation with $P=(0,0)$, $Q=(8,0)$: $R\\approx(10.02,\\,5.65)$, $S\\approx(2.02,\\,5.65)$; the bisector meets the circle at $A\\approx(3.94,\\,2.92)$ and $B\\approx(9.39,\\,-4.81)$, so $AB\\approx9.5$ cm."],"answer":"$AB\\approx9.5$ cm","figs":["w13-parallelogram"]},{"title":"A restaurant plan","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"The floor of a restaurant is a quadrilateral $ABCD$ with $AB=6$ m, $BC=7.5$ m, $AD=5$ m, $\\angle DAB=105^\\circ$ and $\\angle ABC=90^\\circ$. (a) Using a scale of 1 cm to 1 m, construct the plan. (b) A washing basin $O$ is equidistant from $BC$ and $CD$ and exactly 5.5 m from $A$. Locate it. (c) Find the perimeter of the floor."}],"steps":["(a) Draw $AB=6$ cm; construct $90^\\circ$ at $B$ and mark $C$ with $BC=7.5$ cm; construct $105^\\circ$ at $A$ and mark $D$ with $AD=5$ cm; join $CD$.","(b) Points equidistant from $BC$ and $CD$ lie on the bisector of $\\angle BCD$. Points 5.5 m from $A$ lie on the circle with centre $A$ and radius 5.5 cm. $O$ is their intersection inside the room.","(c) $CD$ measures about 7.8 cm. Check: with $A=(0,0)$, $C=(6,\\,7.5)$ and $D=(5\\cos105^\\circ,\\,5\\sin105^\\circ)=(-1.29,\\,4.83)$: $CD=\\sqrt{7.29^2+2.67^2}\\approx7.77$ m.","Perimeter $\\approx6+7.5+7.77+5=26.3$ m.","By calculation, $O\\approx(3.64,\\,4.12)$: about 2.4 m from both $BC$ and $CD$."],"answer":"(c) about 26.3 m; $O$ is about 2.4 m from walls $BC$ and $CD$","figs":["w13-restaurant"]},{"title":"Siting a market","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Town $M$ is 20 km from $N$ and 22 km from $P$, and $N$ is 18 km from $P$. A market must be equidistant from $N$ and $M$ and exactly 10 km from $P$. (a) Using a scale of 1 cm to 2 km, find by construction the possible sites $A$ and $B$. (b) Find the distance between the sites. (c) Find their distances from $N$. (d) Which site is more convenient? Justify."}],"steps":["(a) Construct triangle $MNP$ by SSS ($NM=10$ cm, $NP=9$ cm, $MP=11$ cm). Construct the perpendicular bisector of $NM$ and the circle with centre $P$ and radius 5 cm. They meet at $A$ and $B$.","Calculation: with $N=(0,0)$ and $M=(20,0)$, $P=(6,\\,16.97)$. The bisector is $x=10$; $(10-6)^2+(y-16.97)^2=100$ gives $y=16.97\\pm9.17$.","(b) $AB=2\\times9.17\\approx18.3$ km.","(c) $A=(10,\\,7.81)$: $AN=\\sqrt{100+60.9}\\approx12.7$ km. $B=(10,\\,26.14)$: $BN\\approx28.0$ km.","(d) Site $A$: it is 12.7 km from both $N$ and $M$ (instead of 28.0 km) and still 10 km from $P$, so total travel is much less."],"answer":"(b) about 18.3 km (c) $AN\\approx12.7$ km, $BN\\approx28.0$ km (d) $A$","figs":["w13-market"]},{"title":"A region of points","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"$ABC$ is an equilateral triangle of side 8 cm. Construct and shade the region $R$ of points inside the triangle that are less than 4 cm from $A$ and nearer to $B$ than to $C$. Find the area of $R$."}],"steps":["Construct the triangle (all arcs of radius 8 cm).","“Less than 4 cm from $A$”: inside the circle with centre $A$, radius 4 cm.","“Nearer to $B$ than to $C$”: on $B$’s side of the perpendicular bisector of $BC$, which passes through $A$ (the triangle is equilateral).","$R$ is the sector of the circle between $AB$ and the bisector: angle $30^\\circ$ at $A$.","Area $=\\dfrac{30}{360}\\times\\pi\\times4^2=\\dfrac{4\\pi}{3}\\approx4.19$ cm²."],"answer":"A $30^\\circ$ sector of radius 4 cm; area about 4.19 cm²","figs":[]}],"summary":[{"title":"Key results","items":["Triangles: SSS, SAS, ASA/AAS, RHS; SSA may give two triangles when $AB\\sin B<AC<AB$.","Quadrilaterals need five pieces of data; use parallel-line and diagonal properties.","Loci: circle (one point), perpendicular bisector (two points), angle bisector (two lines), midline (two parallel lines), parallel pair (one line), circumcentre (three points).","Points satisfying two conditions lie at intersections of loci; inequalities give regions.","Check scale drawings with the sine and cosine rules or coordinates."]}],"quiz":[{"q":"Which set of lengths cannot form a triangle?","options":["3 cm, 4 cm, 8 cm","5 cm, 6 cm, 7 cm","4 cm, 4 cm, 7 cm","6 cm, 8 cm, 10 cm"],"correct":0,"explain":"$3+4<8$."},{"q":"The locus of points equidistant from two points $A$ and $B$ is","options":["the perpendicular bisector of $AB$","the circle with diameter $AB$","the line $AB$","the bisector of an angle at $A$"],"correct":0,"explain":"Every point on it is the same distance from $A$ and $B$."},{"q":"The locus of points 3 cm from a fixed point $P$ is","options":["a circle of radius 3 cm centred at $P$","a line 3 cm from $P$","a square of side 3 cm","two parallel lines"],"correct":0,"explain":"Constant distance from one point."},{"q":"The locus of points equidistant from two intersecting lines is","options":["the bisectors of the angles between them","a circle","a line parallel to both","the perpendicular bisector of one line"],"correct":0,"explain":"Angle bisectors."},{"q":"In a trapezium $ABCD$ with $AD\\parallel BC$ and $\\angle ABC=110^\\circ$, $\\angle BAD=$","options":["$70^\\circ$","$110^\\circ$","$90^\\circ$","$55^\\circ$"],"correct":0,"explain":"Co-interior angles sum to $180^\\circ$."},{"q":"The point equidistant from three villages is found by intersecting","options":["two perpendicular bisectors","two angle bisectors","two medians","two altitudes"],"correct":0,"explain":"It is the circumcentre."},{"q":"Given $AB=10$, $\\angle B=30^\\circ$ and $AC=7$, the number of possible triangles is","options":["2","1","0","3"],"correct":0,"explain":"$10\\sin30^\\circ=5<7<10$."},{"q":"A rhombus has side 5 cm and one diagonal 8 cm. The other diagonal is","options":["6 cm","3 cm","4 cm","9.4 cm"],"correct":0,"explain":"$2\\sqrt{25-16}$."},{"q":"The region “nearer to $B$ than to $C$” is bounded by","options":["the perpendicular bisector of $BC$","the circle on $BC$ as diameter","the line $BC$","the bisector of angle $B$"],"correct":0,"explain":"Points on the bisector are equally near both."},{"q":"A goat tied to the middle of a 6 m straight rail by a 2 m rope can reach a region bounded by","options":["two parallel segments and two semicircles","a circle of radius 2 m","a circle of radius 8 m","a rectangle 6 m by 2 m"],"correct":0,"explain":"Points within 2 m of a segment."}],"exercise":[{"q":"Construct triangle $LMN$ with $LM=7$ cm, $MN=8$ cm and $LN=9$ cm. Calculate the largest angle.","a":"Opposite $LN$: $\\cos M=\\tfrac{49+64-81}{112}$, $M\\approx73.4^\\circ$"},{"q":"Construct triangle $ABC$ with $AB=9$ cm, $\\angle A=60^\\circ$ and $AC=6$ cm. Calculate $BC$.","a":"$BC^2=81+36-54=63$: $BC\\approx7.94$ cm"},{"q":"Construct triangle $PQR$ with $PQ=10$ cm, $\\angle P=45^\\circ$, $\\angle Q=75^\\circ$. Calculate $QR$.","a":"$\\angle R=60^\\circ$: $QR=\\tfrac{10\\sin45^\\circ}{\\sin60^\\circ}\\approx8.16$ cm"},{"q":"For $AB=9$ cm, $AC=7$ cm and $\\angle B=35^\\circ$, show that two triangles are possible and find both values of $\\angle C$.","a":"$9\\sin35^\\circ\\approx5.16<7<9$; $\\sin C\\approx0.737$: $47.5^\\circ$ or $132.5^\\circ$"},{"q":"Construct parallelogram $ABCD$ with $AB=7$ cm, $AD=5$ cm and $\\angle DAB=60^\\circ$. Calculate both diagonals.","a":"$BD=\\sqrt{39}\\approx6.24$ cm, $AC=\\sqrt{109}\\approx10.44$ cm"},{"q":"Construct a rhombus with diagonals 8 cm and 6 cm. Find its side and angles.","a":"5 cm; $2\\tan^{-1}\\tfrac34\\approx73.7^\\circ$ and $106.3^\\circ$"},{"q":"Construct trapezium $PQRS$ with $PQ\\parallel SR$, $PQ=9$ cm, $\\angle P=60^\\circ$, $PS=5$ cm and $SR=5$ cm. Calculate $QR$.","a":"$S=(2.5,\\,4.33)$, $R=(7.5,\\,4.33)$: $QR=\\sqrt{1.5^2+4.33^2}\\approx4.58$ cm"},{"q":"Two trees are 30 m apart. Describe the locus of points equidistant from them and the locus of points 20 m from the first tree, and find the distance between the two points that satisfy both.","a":"Perpendicular bisector and circle: $2\\sqrt{20^2-15^2}\\approx26.5$ m"},{"q":"In triangle $ABC$ with $AB=8$, $BC=7$, $CA=6$ cm, construct the point equidistant from $A$, $B$ and $C$, and calculate the radius of the circle through them.","a":"$R=\\dfrac{a}{2\\sin A}$; $\\cos A=\\tfrac{64+36-49}{96}$, $A\\approx57.9^\\circ$: $R\\approx4.13$ cm"},{"q":"A security light at a corner of a 20 m by 12 m yard lights everything within 15 m. What fraction of the yard is lit? Describe the region.","a":"A triangle (area 54 m²) plus a $53.1^\\circ$ sector of radius 15 m (area 104.3 m²): 158.3 m², about 66% of the yard"},{"q":"Construct the region inside a square of side 6 cm that is nearer to side $AB$ than to side $AD$ and more than 3 cm from $C$.","a":"Region on $AB$’s side of the diagonal $AC$, outside the circle of radius 3 about $C$; area $18-\\tfrac{9\\pi}{8}\\approx14.47$ cm²"},{"q":"Points $A$ and $B$ are 10 cm apart. Find the area of the region of points less than 6 cm from both $A$ and $B$.","a":"Lens of two circles: $2(36\\cos^{-1}\\tfrac56-5\\sqrt{11})\\approx9.0$ cm²"}],"theory":[{"q":"(a) Using ruler and compasses only, construct triangle $ABC$ with $AB=10$ cm, $\\angle ABC=60^\\circ$ and $BC=7$ cm. (b) Construct the locus of points equidistant from $A$ and $C$, and the locus of points equidistant from $AB$ and $BC$. (c) Label their intersection $X$ and measure $BX$. (d) Calculate $AC$ and $BX$.","steps":[],"answer":"","model":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Draw $AB=10$ cm, construct $60^\\circ$ at $B$ and mark $C$ at 7 cm."},{"k":"p","text":"(b) The perpendicular bisector of $AC$, and the bisector of $\\angle ABC$."},{"k":"p","text":"(c), (d) $AC^2=100+49-70=79$, so $AC\\approx8.89$ cm. Take $B=(0,0)$, $A=(10,0)$ and $C=(3.5,\\,6.06)$. The angle bisector at $B$ makes $30^\\circ$ with $BA$, so $X=(0.866t,\\,0.5t)$ where $t=BX$. Setting $XA^2=XC^2$: $t^2-17.32t+100=t^2-12.12t+49$, so $5.20t=51$ and $t\\approx9.81$. Hence $BX\\approx9.8$ cm, which the measurement should match."}]},{"q":"A village water committee wants a borehole that is equidistant from the school $S$ and the clinic $C$, which are 600 m apart, and within 400 m of the chief’s palace $P$, which is 500 m from $S$ and 700 m from $C$. (a) Using a scale of 1 cm to 100 m, construct triangle $SCP$. (b) Construct the locus of points equidistant from $S$ and $C$ and the region within 400 m of $P$. (c) Describe where the borehole may be placed, and find the nearest such point to $S$.","steps":[],"answer":"","model":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Draw $SC=6$ cm and arcs of 5 cm from $S$ and 7 cm from $C$ to locate $P$."},{"k":"p","text":"(b) The perpendicular bisector of $SC$ and the disc of radius 4 cm centred at $P$."},{"k":"p","text":"(c) The borehole may be anywhere on the part of the perpendicular bisector inside the circle. With $S=(0,0)$, $C=(6,0)$: $P=(1,\\,4.90)$ (since $x^2+y^2=25$, $(x-6)^2+y^2=49$ gives $x=1$). The bisector $x=3$ meets the circle where $(y-4.90)^2=16-4=12$, $y=4.90\\pm3.46$: from $(3,\\,1.44)$ to $(3,\\,8.36)$. The nearest point to $S$ is $(3,\\,1.44)$: about $\\sqrt{9+2.07}\\approx3.33$ cm, that is 333 m from $S$ (and from $C$)."}]},{"q":"(a) Explain why the angle-bisector construction gives the locus of points equidistant from two intersecting lines. (b) Explain why the bisectors of the four angles formed by two crossing lines form two perpendicular lines. (c) Hence describe the locus of points equidistant from three lines that form a triangle, inside the triangle.","steps":[],"answer":"","model":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Let $X$ be on the bisector of $\\angle AOB$. Drop perpendiculars $XM$ and $XN$ to the arms. Triangles $OMX$ and $ONX$ have $\\angle M=\\angle N=90^\\circ$, $\\angle MOX=\\angle NOX$ and $OX$ common, so they are congruent (AAS) and $XM=XN$."},{"k":"p","text":"(b) Adjacent angles at the crossing add up to $180^\\circ$; their bisectors make $\\tfrac12$ of each, so the angle between the bisectors is $\\tfrac12\\times180^\\circ=90^\\circ$."},{"k":"p","text":"(c) A point equidistant from all three sides lies on the bisectors of all three angles. Inside the triangle this is a single point, the incentre, the centre of the inscribed circle (Week 11)."}]},{"q":"(a) Construct quadrilateral $ABCD$ with $AB=8$ cm, $\\angle DAB=90^\\circ$, $AD=6$ cm, $\\angle ABC=75^\\circ$ and $BC=7$ cm. (b) Measure $CD$ and $\\angle BCD$. (c) Construct the locus of points within 3 cm of $D$ and the locus of points equidistant from $AB$ and $AD$, and shade the region inside $ABCD$ that is within 3 cm of $D$ and nearer to $AB$ than to $AD$.","steps":[],"answer":"","model":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Draw $AB=8$ cm; construct $90^\\circ$ at $A$ and mark $D$ at 6 cm; construct $75^\\circ$ at $B$ and mark $C$ at 7 cm; join $CD$."},{"k":"p","text":"(b) With $A=(0,0)$, $B=(8,0)$, $D=(0,6)$ and $C=(8-7\\cos75^\\circ,\\,7\\sin75^\\circ)=(6.19,\\,6.76)$: $CD=\\sqrt{6.19^2+0.76^2}\\approx6.24$ cm. At $C$, $\\cos\\angle BCD=\\dfrac{\\vec{CB}\\cdot\\vec{CD}}{|CB||CD|}=\\dfrac{(1.81)(-6.19)+(-6.76)(-0.76)}{7\\times6.24}\\approx-0.139$, so $\\angle BCD\\approx98^\\circ$ (and $\\angle ADC\\approx97^\\circ$; check: $90+75+98+97=360$)."},{"k":"p","text":"(c) The circle of radius 3 cm about $D$; the bisector of the right angle at $A$ (the line $y=x$). The region is the part of the disc about $D$ below the line $y=x$ and inside $ABCD$."}]},{"q":"A circular water tank must be built on a rectangular plot $PQRS$, 40 m by 30 m, so that its centre is (i) equidistant from $PQ$ and $PS$ (ii) 25 m from $R$. (c) What is the largest radius the tank can have if it must stay inside the plot?","steps":[],"answer":"","model":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Draw the rectangle $8$ cm by $6$ cm. Only $(18.04,\\,18.04)$ lies inside the plot."},{"k":"p","text":"(c) The centre is 18.04 m from $PQ$ and $PS$, $40-18.04=21.96$ m from $QR$ and $30-18.04=11.96$ m from $RS$.
